_tuning_notes: Savanna/badlands tortoise. worldgen_only true = Untamed Wilds style: spawns with newly generated chunks only, never naturally respawns — killing them permanently empties the area, and they drop nothing. shell_armor/shell_ticks tune the retreat (+8 armor, immobile, 10s). Breeds with sweet berries (breed_item), never tames. RARITY: tier 'uncommon' supplies the spawn weight; group_size and nearby_cap are pinned here (1-3, cap 4). nearby_cap denies natural spawns when that many of this animal are already within 64 blocks — the fix for persistent CREATURE mobs accumulating forever. ECOLOGY 0.4.2: gained the arid and beach families the spec calls for (desert via #c:is_desert so Terralith deserts count; beaches minus snowy). BABY SIZE 0.4.2: baby_scale moved 0.5 -> 1.0. The client already bakes the baby mesh through vanilla's BabyModelTransform (body halved, head full size) and vanilla age scaling halves the hitbox, so a 0.5 here was a SECOND shrink and calves rendered at a quarter of adult size. 1.0 = vanilla baby proportions. TERRALITH PASS: excludes Terralith's snowy_badlands (a cold-blooded reptile). SIZE PASS 0.4.6: scale set against MEASURED vanilla hitboxes rather than by eye (cow 0.90x1.40, horse 1.40x1.60, polar bear 1.40x1.40, ravager 1.95x2.20, wolf 0.60x0.85, turtle 1.20x0.40, ocelot 0.60x0.70, chicken 0.40x0.70). Attributes.SCALE is uniform and multiplies the MODEL and the HITBOX together, so this is the one lever that cannot desync them. 1.04x turtle width. NOTE: uniform scale raises height with width, so this is proportionally taller than a vanilla turtle; a genuinely flat shell needs a mesh change. SIZE PASS revised: the first attempt scaled an already-wrong box. Measuring the baked meshes showed the hitboxes never matched the models — the hippo mesh was 1.06 blocks tall inside a 1.60 box (66% fill, a third of it empty air), while the gorilla mesh was LARGER than its hitbox (121%). Builder dimensions in MenagerieEntities now match the measured mesh, and this scale multiplies model and hitbox together from there, so the drawn animal fills the box it is struck in.
